Organ: Muddy or Clear? (A/B)

Four switches on the band’s tonewheel organ, one possible cause of mud each, to find by ear which ones matter.

The band’s tonewheel organ was said to sound muddy next to other clonewheels. Each switch below turns one fix on or off. A loop of comping chords plays over a bass line, as in the band. Switch one thing at a time and listen. All the “after” values are first guesses (2026-11-27); nobody has listened yet.

The switches

On Fix Before After
Registration with the 4′ in 888000000 888400000
Less bass lift as the swell closes 7 dB 2 dB
Less tube drive 1.5 0.9
Horn presence peak none +4 dB at 2.5 kHz

What each one is

  • Registration. 16′, 5⅓′ and 8′ full and nothing higher sits in the bass player’s range and the low mids. Adding the 4′ gives the chords an edge.
  • Swell bass lift. The pedal model lifts 160 Hz by up to 7 dB as it closes (a guess in ORGAN.md). The band’s organist keeps it between 0.48 and 0.90.
  • Drive. The tube stage distorts dense low chords into low intermodulation.
  • Horn peak. A real Leslie horn has a presence peak; ours was flat above the 800 Hz crossover.

Settings here last only while the page is open; when we know which fixes help, they go into the organ’s definition in apps/shared/band/sounds.js.
